'''''Avatar: The Last Airbender''''', also known as '''''Avatar Legends''''',<ref>{{Cite book |title=''[[Avatar Legends: The Roleplaying Game]]'' (Core Book) |date=October 26, 2022 |publisher=[[Magpie Games]] |page=6 |quote=Originally, this setting was only a single show—''Avatar: The Last Airbender''—that told the story of Avatar Aang's journey to master the four elements and save the world. But this world's history spans thousands of years, and over time, many more of its stories across multiple eras of Avatars have been told—including comics, novels, and of course, the epic series featuring Aang's successor, ''The Legend of Korra''. Together, these works make up ''Avatar Legends'', a broad term for all of the different stories that detail the adventures of heroes of the Four Nations (and Republic City).}}</ref> is an American [[multimedia franchise]] created by [[Michael Dante DiMartino]] and [[Bryan Konietzko]]. The franchise began with the animated television series ''[[Avatar: The Last Airbender]]'', which aired on [[Nickelodeon]] from 2005 to 2008. The franchise is set in an Asian-inspired<ref name="vanityfairremake">{{cite web|last=Bradley|first=Laura|date=September 18, 2018|title=Netflix Is Making a Live-Action Avatar: The Last Airbender, Promises Not to Mess It Up|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2018/09/avatar-the-last-airbender-live-action-remake-netflix|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004093853/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2018/09/avatar-the-last-airbender-live-action-remake-netflix|archive-date=October 4, 2018|access-date=October 4, 2018|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]}}</ref> [[fantasy world]] in which some people can [[telekinesis|telekinetically]] manipulate (or "bend") one of the four [[classical element]]s: air, water, earth, or fire. Only the [[Title character|titular]] "Avatar" can bend all four elements and is responsible for maintaining balance in the world.<ref name=speakeasy>{{cite web|last=Farley|first=Christopher John|title='The Last Airbender: Legend of Korra': The Creators Speak|url=https://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2011/03/08/the-last-airbender-legend-of-korra-the-creators-speak/|work=Speakeasy|date=March 8, 2011|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120524154510/http://blogs.wsj.com/speakeasy/2011/03/08/the-last-airbender-legend-of-korra-the-creators-speak/|archive-date=May 24, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsweek.com/avatar-last-airbender-netflix-release-date-series-original-new-whitewashed-1127230|title=New 'Avatar: The Last Airbender' Series on Netflix: Original Creators Promise 'Non-Whitewashed' Cast|work=[[Newsweek]]|date=September 18, 2018|first=Autumn Noel|last=Kelly|access-date=October 8, 2018|archive-date=October 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008164143/https://www.newsweek.com/avatar-last-airbender-netflix-release-date-series-original-new-whitewashed-1127230|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Avatar'' is a franchise spanning works in various forms of [[Media (communication)|media]]. A sequel animated series to ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'', ''[[The Legend of Korra]]'', ran from 2012 to 2014. The storylines of both animated series have been continued in comic book form.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/avatar-the-last-airbender-kyoshi-novels/|title=Avatar Kyoshi's life will be explored in 2 young adult novels|work=[[The Daily Dot]]|first=Michelle|last=Jaworski|date=August 30, 2018|access-date=October 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008150026/https://www.dailydot.com/parsec/avatar-the-last-airbender-kyoshi-novels/|archive-date=October 8, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=kyoshinovelew/> Other franchise [[tie-in]]s include [[novelization]]s, [[Coffee_table_book#As_media_tie-in_publications|art book]]s, companion books, video games, and [[home video|home media]] releases. In 2010, the first season of the original animated series was adapted into a [[live-action]] film titled ''[[The Last Airbender (film)|The Last Airbender]]''. A [[Avatar: The Last Airbender (2024 TV series)|live-action television remake]] of the original series, also named ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'', was co-produced by [[Netflix]] and premiered in 2024.

In February 2021, Nickelodeon announced the formation of [[Avatar Studios]], a division dedicated to the creation of ''Avatar'' projects. The first project, an animated sequel film titled ''[[Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender]]'', released in July 2026. A second sequel series, ''[[Avatar: Seven Havens]]'', premiered in October 2026.

==Premise==
The franchise is set in an Asian-inspired fantasy world that is divided into four nations: the Water Tribes, the Fire Nation, the Air Nomads, and the Earth Kingdom. People of each nation are capable of [[telekinetically]] manipulating (referred to as "bending" in the franchise) one of the four [[Classical element|elements]]: water, earth, fire, or air.

The titular "Avatar" is the only person who can bend all four elements, and they are responsible for maintaining spiritual and physical balance in the world. After an Avatar's death, the Avatar Spirit, Raava, is reborn into a new person of a different nation, who is the new Avatar and who must master the bending arts of the four elements, and take on their Avatar responsibilities.

===Animated series===
====''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' (2005–2008)====
{{main|Avatar: The Last Airbender|l1=''Avatar: The Last Airbender''|List of Avatar: The Last Airbender episodes|l2=List of ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' episodes}}

The first series in the franchise, ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' follows the young Avatar [[Aang]] as he attempts to end the Fire Nation's war of conquest against the other three nations. Aang, who is the last surviving Air Nomad due to a [[genocide]] perpetrated by the Fire Nation, is joined by a teenage waterbender of the Southern Water Tribe, [[Katara (Avatar: The Last Airbender)|Katara]], her non-bending brother [[Sokka]], and later the young blind earthbending prodigy [[Toph Beifong|Toph]], as he journeys to master bending the elements so that he can defeat the Fire Nation's leader, [[Ozai (Avatar: The Last Airbender)|Fire Lord Ozai]], and restore peace throughout the four nations. The series also depicts the journey of Prince [[Zuko]], Ozai's disgraced and exiled son, as he tries to restore his honor. When Ozai exiled him, he sent him on a quest to find the Avatar, a task thought impossible at the time. Zuko stays devoted to capturing Aang throughout the first season, but would go on to join Aang’s group later in the series.

====''The Legend of Korra'' (2012–2014)====
{{main|The Legend of Korra|l1=''The Legend of Korra''|List of The Legend of Korra episodes|l2=List of ''The Legend of Korra'' episodes}}

Set 70 years after the original series, ''The Legend of Korra'' follows Aang's successor as the Avatar, a waterbender from the Southern Water Tribe named [[Korra (The Last Airbender: Legend of Korra character)|Korra]], who moves to the new, multi-ethnic Republic City to learn airbending from Aang's youngest son, [[Tenzin (The Legend of Korra)|Tenzin]]. She befriends a firebending and earthbending pair of brothers, [[Mako (The Legend of Korra)|Mako]] and [[Bolin (The Legend of Korra)|Bolin]], and the industrial heiress [[Asami Sato]], and contends with a series of political upheavals, including a rising anti-bending movement, a civil war in the Water Tribes, an [[anarchist]] conspiracy, and the rise of an authoritarian government in the Earth Kingdom.

====''Avatar: Seven Havens'' (2026–present) ====
{{main|Avatar: Seven Havens|l1=''Avatar: Seven Havens''}}

In celebration of the 20th anniversary of ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'', [[Nickelodeon]] and [[Avatar Studios]] announced ''[[Avatar: Seven Havens]]'', a new 2D animated series. Set 225 years after the events of ''The Legend of Korra'', ''Avatar: Seven Havens'' takes place in the aftermath of a global cataclysmic event, with civilization on the verge of collapse. The series follows Korra's successor as the Avatar, Pavi, an earthbender who is blamed for humanity's destruction and attempts to survive with help from her long-lost twin sibling named Nisha.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/news/616866/avatar-seven-havens-nickelodeon-konietzko-dimartino |title=Nickelodeon's next Avatar animated series is finally coming together |last=Pulliam-Moore |first=Charles  |website=[[TheVerge]] |date=February 20, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Romano | first=Nick | title='Avatar: Seven Havens' first look reveals the next earthbending Avatar | website=Entertainment Weekly | date=July 24, 2025 | url=https://ew.com/avatar-seven-havens-first-look-reveals-earthbending-avatar-mentor-11778575 | access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref> The series was created by [[Michael Dante DiMartino]] and [[Bryan Konietzko]], and [[Ethan Spaulding]] and Sehaj Sethi serve as executive producers. ''Seven Havens'' consists of 26 half-hour episodes spread across two seasons, or books.<ref name="Havens2027">{{cite web |date=1 May 2025 |title=Avatar: Seven Havens Officially Announced, Set After the Events of The Legend of Korra |url=https://www.nickalive.net/2025/05/avatar-seven-havens-slated-to-premiere.html |access-date=1 May 2025 |website=[[NickAlive]]}}</ref> On December 23, 2025, it was announced the series would be released on [[Paramount+]].<ref name="Paramount+" /> On July 23, 2026, it was announced at [[San Diego Comic-Con]] that the series would premiere on October 9.<ref name="SevenHavensPremiere">{{Cite web|last=Gomez|first=Dessi|title=‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Sets Premiere Date On Paramount+; Unveils Teaser Trailer|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/avatar-seven-havens-release-date-teaser-paramount-1237001889/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=July 23, 2026|access-date=July 23, 2026}}</ref> ''Seven Havens'' is set to conclude after its fourth season.<ref name="IGNFinaleQuestions">{{cite web |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/avatar-seven-havens-finale-showrunners-ending-explained-biggest-questions |title=Avatar: Seven Havens Showrunners Address Your Biggest Finale Burning Questions |website=[[IGN]] |first=Alex |last=Zalben |date=October 31, 2026 |access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref>

==== ''Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos'' ====
On October 9, 2026, alongside the announcement of ''Seven Havens'' being renewed for additional seasons, a new animated series was given a production order for Paramount+. Described as an action comedy, it is a prequel set before Aang's story about a 14 year old Kuruk during a time of peace.<ref name="Kuruk">{{Cite web |last=White |first=Abbey |date=2026-10-09 |title=‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Renewed for Two More Seasons, ‘Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos’ Series Announced at NYCC |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/avatar-seven-havens-renewed-kuruk-wave-of-chaos-series-1236726315/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}}</ref> Co-creator Bryan Konietzko will be showrunning the series.<ref>{{cite web|last=Otterson|first=Joe|date=9 October 2026|title='Avatar: Seven Havens' Renewed for Seasons 3 and 4 at Paramount+|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/avatar-seven-havens-renewed-season-3-4-paramount-1236906480/|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=9 October 2026}}</ref>

====''The Last Airbender'' (2010)====
{{main|The Last Airbender (film)|l1=''The Last Airbender'' (film)}}

''The Last Airbender'' is a 2010 live-action adaptation of [[Avatar: The Last Airbender season 1|the first season]] of the animated series ''[[Avatar: The Last Airbender]]'' by [[M. Night Shyamalan]]. The film was widely panned by critics and fans of the animated series, and has since been considered [[List of films considered the worst|one of the worst films ever made]] and took in $319 million at the worldwide [[box office]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/avatar-last-airbender-netflix-show-better-shyamalan-movie/|title=Netflix's Avatar: The Last Airbender Can Make Up For Shyamalan's Failure|publisher=[[Screen Rant]]|date=September 19, 2018|first=Molly|last=Freeman|access-date=October 8, 2018|archive-date=October 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181008133008/https://screenrant.com/avatar-last-airbender-netflix-show-better-shyamalan-movie/|url-status=live}}</ref>

as Aang, [[Dionne Quan]] as Toph, [[Jessica Matten]] as Katara, Román Zaragoza as Sokka, and [[Dave Bautista]] as an antagonist.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/aang-the-last-airbender-first-movie-avatar-trilogy-eric-nam-dave-bautista-8630272|title=Aang: The Last Airbender, the first animated movie in Avatar trilogy, will follow Aang as an adult|last=Wang|first=Jessica|date=April 11, 2024|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=April 11, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Graves |first=Sabina |date=2024-04-11 |title=Aang: The Last Airbender Movie Has Found Its Cast, Including Dave Bautista |url=https://gizmodo.com/last-airbender-animated-trilogy-aang-first-movie-2025-1851404099 |access-date=2024-04-11 |website=[[Gizmodo]]}}</ref> The film was originally set to be released theatrically on October 9, 2026 by [[Paramount Pictures]].<ref name="variety2024">{{Cite web |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=2024-04-18 |title='Aang: The Last Airbender' Delayed to 2026, 'Transformers One' Moves Back a Week |url=https://variety.com/2024/film/news/aang-the-last-airbender-release-date-delays-2026-1235974936/ |access-date=2024-04-18 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> In April 2025, the title of the film was announced as ''The Legend of Aang: The Last Airbender''.<ref name="NewTitle">{{Cite web |last=Fuster |first=Jeremy |date=April 3, 2025 |title='Avatar: The Last Airbender' Film Gets New Title |url=https://www.thewrap.com/avatar-the-last-airbender-movie-new-title/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250403174941/https://www.thewrap.com/avatar-the-last-airbender-movie-new-title/ |archive-date=April 3, 2025 |access-date=April 3, 2025 |website=[[TheWrap]]}}</ref> On December 23, 2025, it was announced the film would instead be released on [[Paramount+]].<ref name="Paramount+">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/legend-of-aang-the-last-airbender-will-skip-theaters-1236457907/|title=''Legend of Aang: The Last Airbender'' Will Skip Theaters and Debut on Paramount+ Alongside New ''Seven Havens'' Series (Exclusive)|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|author=Pamela McClintock|date=December 23, 2025|access-date=December 29, 2025}}</ref> In March 2026, Montgomery revealed that production had wrapped and the final cut of the film had been screened for the entire cast and crew. Posts from the screening by Eric Nam and Román Zaragoza revealed that the film had been retitled ''Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender''. In April 2026, the entire film was leaked on social media platform [[X (social network)|X]]. Investigations were underway by Paramount Pictures to determine the source of the leak. Sources familiar with the situation say the company determined it did not originate internally.<ref name="MovieLeak">{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/legend-of-aang-last-airbender-leak-investigation-paramount-1236723624/|title=Paramount Investigates ‘The Legend of Aang: The Last Airbender’ Leak, Determines It Didn’t Come From Studio|work=[[Variety (magazine)]]|last1=Tangcay|first1=Jazz|last2=Maddaus|first2=Gene|date=April 16, 2026|access-date=April 17, 2026}}</ref> ''Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender'' was released on Paramount+ on July 25, 2026, with a limited theatrical release in [[Los Angeles]] and [[New York City]].<ref name="ReleaseJul2026">{{Cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |date=July 7, 2026 |title='Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' Moves Up Release Date to July, Drops Intense First Trailer |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/avatar-aang-the-last-airbender-release-date-july-trailer-1236802799/ |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=July 7, 2026}}</ref>. The film received generally positive reviews from critics, fans, and audiences.

== Other media ==

=== Podcast ===
''Avatar: Braving the Elements'' is a podcast by Nickelodeon in which [[Dante Basco]], the voice actor for [[Prince Zuko]], and [[Janet Varney]], who voiced [[Korra]], revisit the animated television series.<ref name="ew2021">{{cite magazine |last=Yang |first=Rachel |date=June 15, 2021 |title=Avatar actors Dante Basco, Janet Varney tease ''Braving the Elements'' podcast in trailer |url=https://ew.com/tv/avatar-the-last-airbender-braving-the-elements-trailer/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The podcast's main focus are deep dives into each TV episode in chronological order; other episodes explore individual characters, important themes in the ''Avatar'' universe or the craft and artistic work which went into creating it. Varney and Basco are often joined by other people who were involved in bringing the series to life, including fellow voice actors, writers, directors, producers and the show creators themselves. ''Avatar: Braving the Elements'' has also featured fans of the show as guests and been live-recorded by its hosts at conventions.<ref name="cbr2022">{{cite web |last=Meszaros |first=E.L. |date=May 3, 2022 |title=Avatar: Braving the Elements' Janet Varney Previews the Podcast's Season 2 |url=https://www.cbr.com/avatar-braving-the-elements-janet-varney-interview/ |access-date=June 4, 2024 |website=[[Comic Book Resources]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="awn2023">{{cite web |last=Sarto |first=Debbie Diamond |date=October 14, 2023 |title=Nick Renews 'Avatar: Braving the Elements' Podcast for Season 3 |url=https://www.awn.com/news/nick-renews-avatar-braving-elements-podcast-season-3 |access-date=June 4, 2024 |website=[[Animation World Network]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="awn2024">{{cite web |last=Sarto |first=Debbie Diamond |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Nickelodeon Drops 'Avatar: Braving the Elements' Podcast Season 3 Trailer |url=https://www.awn.com/news/nickelodeon-drops-avatar-braving-elements-podcast-season-3-trailer |access-date=June 4, 2024 |website=[[Animation World Network]] |language=en}}</ref> Beginning with season 3, video recordings of the podcast were uploaded to Youtube.<ref name="TeamAvatarYT">{{cite web |last1=Basco |first1=Dante |last2=Varney |first2=Janet |date=2024 |title=Avatar: Braving the Elements Podcast |url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL0uuU7hMyKdWNLPdOQaDmLxnm-WGfmSxC |access-date=June 4, 2024 |website=youtube.com |publisher=Avatar: The Last Airbender |language=en |format=video}}</ref>

=== Tabletop roleplaying game ===
{{Main|Avatar Legends: The Roleplaying Game{{!}}''Avatar Legends: The Roleplaying Game''}}

On July 12, 2021, Magpie Games announced that on August 3 of the same year they'd be launching a [[Kickstarter]] campaign for ''Avatar Legends: The Roleplaying Game'', an officially licensed tabletop roleplaying game set in the universe of ''Avatar: The Last Airbender'' and ''The Legend of Korra''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avatar Legends RPG on Kickstarter Aug 3rd! |url=https://magpiegames.com/blogs/news/avatar-legends-the-roleplaying-game-kickstarter-august-3-2021 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920174042/https://magpiegames.com/blogs/news/avatar-legends-the-roleplaying-game-kickstarter-august-3-2021 |archive-date=September 20, 2022 |access-date=December 8, 2021}}</ref> The campaign raised [[USD]] $9.53M, becoming the most successful campaign for a tabletop game in Kickstarter's history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2021 |title=Avatar Legends Has Been So Successful It's Run Out of Stretch Goals |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/avatar-legends-stretch-goals-run-out |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211209194758/https://www.ign.com/articles/avatar-legends-stretch-goals-run-out |archive-date=December 9, 2021 |access-date=December 8, 2021}}</ref> Pre-orders for much of the game's content opened on October 12, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 7, 2022 |title=Magpie Games Announces Preorder and Upcoming Product Release Schedule for Avatar Legends: The Roleplaying Game at New York Comic Con |url=https://magpiegames.com/blogs/avatar-legends-the-rpg/magpie-games-announces-preorder-and-upcoming-product-release-schedule-for-avatar-legends-the-roleplaying-game-at-new-york-comic-con |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221214074521/https://magpiegames.com/blogs/avatar-legends-the-rpg/magpie-games-announces-preorder-and-upcoming-product-release-schedule-for-avatar-legends-the-roleplaying-game-at-new-york-comic-con |archive-date=December 14, 2022 |access-date=December 13, 2022}}</ref>

=== Concert ===
{{Main|Avatar: The Last Airbender in Concert|l1 = ''Avatar: The Last Airbender in Concert''}}

In October 2023, Nickelodeon and GEA Live announced ''Avatar: The Last Airbender in Concert'', an ongoing concert tour featuring Zuckerman's score for the series.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web |last=Dar |first=Taimur |date=October 17, 2023 |title=Experience the music of AVATAR: THE LAST Airbender in concert |url=https://www.comicsbeat.com/avatar-the-last-airbender-in-concert-announced/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240509184042/https://www.comicsbeat.com/avatar-the-last-airbender-in-concert-announced/ |archive-date=May 9, 2024 |access-date=May 25, 2024 |website=The Beat |language=en-US}}</ref> The tour was initially announced for four dates and locations in the UK, US, and France, and premiered in [[London]] on January 21, 2024.<ref name=":16" /><ref name=":22">{{Cite web |last=Periccos |first=Jack |date=January 22, 2024 |title=Avatar: The Last Airbender In Concert |url=https://www.music-news.com/review/UK/15757/Live/Avatar-The-Last-Airbender-In-Concert-Royal-Festival-Hall |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240525164344/https://www.music-news.com/review/UK/15757/Live/Avatar-The-Last-Airbender-In-Concert-Royal-Festival-Hall |archive-date=May 25, 2024 |access-date=May 25, 2024 |website=Music-News.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The concert runs for over two hours and the music is performed by an orchestral ensemble, while several moments from the === Trading Card Game ===
On October 28th, 2025, [[Wizards of the Coast]] announced their newest ''[[Magic: The Gathering|Magic the Gathering]]'' crossover to be with ''Avatar: The Last Airbender''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Collecting Magic: The Gathering® {{!}} Avatar: The Last Airbender™: The Four Most Important Things to Know |url=https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/collecting-avatar-the-last-airbender |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=MAGIC: THE GATHERING |language=en-US}}</ref> The series was released on November 21st, 2025, with a set of 414 cards; an additional eternal release releasing soon after while providing more artwork and some rereleases of cards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magic: The Gathering {{!}} Avatar: The Last Airbender TLA {{!}} 414 cards (English) {{!}} Magic: The Gathering |url=https://gatherer.wizards.com/sets/TLA |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=Magic: The Gathering Card Database |language=en}}</ref> On November 17th, 2025 a secret lair, a handful of cards, was also released.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Secret Lair: Avatar: The Last Airbender™ Superdrop |url=https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/announcements/secret-lair-avatar-the-last-airbender-superdrop |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=MAGIC: THE GATHERING |language=en-US}}</ref>
